evidence_quotes.quote: This research work aims to explore the current coverage and performance of on-site sanitation facilities based on the use of ABR units in urban Malang and to identify current hurdles affecting the long-term sustainability and impact of decentralized sanitation services.

Grab samples were taken from the inﬂuent and efﬂuent of 23 decentralized wastewater treatment systems using ABR units, which were spread over ﬁve districts in Malang City. Selected ABRs were chosen based on their structure performance.

The service provided by the decentralized system covers less than 5% of the total population in Malang city with a distribution of coverage per district as follows: Blimbing, 1.78%; Kedungkandan, 2.7%; Klojen, 1.5%; Lowokwaru, 1.89%; and Sukun, 1.89%

Figure 5 reveals that the actual daily ﬂow rate of wastewater treated in 98% of the ABR units monitored was still lower than the average design ﬂow rate, which was mainly due to the lower number of users connected. This situation was prevalent due to the discrepancy between the infrastructure provided by the local government (i.e., decentralized sewerage and wastewater treatment facilities) and expectations from the community (i.e., it was expected that the community undertake the work required to connect households to the sewer network).

In general, the quality of the efﬂuent from ABR units in Malang does not meet the quality standards set in the regulations issued by the Ministry of Environment and Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia (Regulation No. P.68/2016).

criterion_notes.c1: Examines community decentralized sanitation coverage in urban Malang using municipal secondary data (reporting city-wide sanitation facility shares, 17% open defecation, <5% district-level ABR user coverage, and under-connection of households to ABR units), alongside its primary focus on anaerobic baffled reactor (ABR) wastewater treatment engineering performance.
criterion_notes.c2: Fails BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, the study is a civil/environmental engineering evaluation of ABR structural condition, hydraulic/organic loading, and pollutant removal efficiency; it does not empirically measure or analyze any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor (Indonesian regulations PERMEN PUPR No. 04/2017 and Ministry of Environment and Forestry Regulation No. P.68/2016 are used solely as technical reactor design criteria and effluent water-quality discharge limits, and brief remarks on SANIMAS community O&M and local expectations for households to finance sewer connections are unmeasured narrative discussion). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, generic SANIMAS decentralized project delivery background and environmental effluent discharge standards are not rule-type mechanisms directly governing household or community service access, and the passing narrative mention of community responsibility/cost for sewer connections is not empirically studied.
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical engineering data (influent and effluent grab sampling of 23 ABR plants across five districts in Malang in March-April 2018 for BOD, TSS, NH4+, TKN, TP, total coliforms, DO, plus dimensional/hydraulic measurements on 17 ABRs) combined with secondary municipal data on 89 ABR plants and city-wide sanitation facilities.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports descriptive secondary outcomes on sanitation access and connection (city-wide toilet facility distribution, district-level ABR population coverage percentages, and actual user-connected wastewater flow vs design capacity across ABR sites), though the primary analytical outcomes are technical reactor structural integrity and pollutant removal efficiency.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the study setting and sample (89 ABR decentralized wastewater treatment plants across five districts in Malang, Indonesia, with 23 sampled for wastewater quality and 17 measured for hydraulic velocity, plus municipal district populations), technical engineering parameters, outcomes, and cross-sectional field monitoring design, though no governance/legal exposure is examined.

study_design: Cross-sectional engineering field performance assessment (influent/effluent grab-sample testing and structural/hydraulic evaluation) combined with descriptive secondary municipal sanitation survey
population_and_sample: Urban Malang, Indonesia (five districts: Blimbing, Kedungkandang, Klojen, Lowokwaru and Sukun): 89 community-scale anaerobic baffled reactor (ABR) decentralized wastewater treatment plants, with hydraulic/dimensional measurements on 17 ABRs and primary influent/effluent grab-sample testing on 23 ABRs, plus city-wide municipal secondary data on household sanitation facilities
exposure: Engineering design, hydraulic/organic loading, and physical structural conditions of ABR wastewater treatment units (no legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance exposure empirically examined)
outcome: Primary: ABR structural condition (Good, Adequate, Bad, Very Bad) and wastewater treatment pollutant removal/effluent quality (BOD, TSS, TKN, NH4+, TP, total coliforms, DO) relative to national discharge standards. Secondary/descriptive: city-wide sanitation facility shares, district-level ABR user coverage (<5%), and connected-user wastewater flow relative to design capacity
rationale: Excluded as E06 (Engineering only). Although the paper includes descriptive municipal secondary statistics on sanitation facility types and ABR user coverage (<5%) in Malang, Indonesia, its empirical investigation is a civil/environmental engineering assessment of anaerobic baffled reactor (ABR) structural integrity, hydraulic/organic loading rates, and pollutant removal efficiency (BOD, TSS, TKN, NH4+, TP, total coliforms, DO). National regulations (PERMEN PUPR No. 04/2017 and Regulation No. P.68/2016) are cited strictly as technical engineering design and effluent water-quality benchmarks, and narrative remarks on SANIMAS community O&M and household sewer-connection expectations are not empirically analyzed under either the plain or narrow 2026-10-13 reading of Criterion 2.
